Privacy Policy

What stays on your device. What an optional cloud backup sends. How you stay in control.

Prepared 26 October 2026 · Publisher: Hussam Alkhatib, Todorbit.

Local by default. No Todorbit account or telemetry is required for local planning. Google Drive backup is optional and experimental in v1.0.13. Google branding verification and full public OAuth policy compliance remain unresolved. No Google approval or compatibility with every account is claimed.

Contact: hussamalkhatib24@gmail.com. Do not send passwords, tokens, passphrases or private backup files.

1. Local planner data

Todorbit stores tasks, notes, events, categories, recurrence, work sessions, habits, goals, history and other planner records in a local SQLite database. Local preferences and backups are also stored on your device. Todorbit does not add analytics or telemetry and does not send planner data to a Todorbit server.

Local databases and recovery files are not encrypted by Todorbit. The optional PIN hides the interface; it is not file encryption. Your operating system, device access and any disk protection you use affect the privacy of local files.

2. Optional Google access

Connecting Google Drive opens Google's official authorization page in your system browser. The pre-release bundles its Desktop application configuration; you do not import a credentials JSON file or configure Google Cloud. Todorbit does not receive your Google password.

The application requests only https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata, to manage its own hidden application-data folder in your Google account. It does not request access to your general Drive files, Gmail, contacts or calendar.

Todorbit reads the connected account's stable permission identifier and, when available, its email address or display name to display the account and guard against accidental account switching. Access and refresh tokens are stored using Windows-protected storage and are associated with the selected local profile. They are not exported in settings or cloud snapshots.

3. What you choose to upload

Cloud uploads occur only when you request them. A full backup contains all SQLite tables plus supported shareable personalization. It can include private notes, event details, archived or deleted records, histories and references to external file paths. The contents of linked external files are not included.

A settings-only backup contains the supported settings categories you select, such as themes, hotkey presets, calendar display, sidebar order and task display, without planner database records. Device-only privacy/PIN policy, Google tokens and widget startup/position controls are excluded from the additional settings payload.

Full cloud backups have a 50 MiB database limit. They are snapshots for backup and restore, not continuous or two-way synchronization.

4. Encryption and Google storage

Before upload, Todorbit encrypts backup contents on your device using AES-256-GCM. The encryption key is derived from your recovery passphrase with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations), using a random salt. Each encryption uses a fresh random nonce and an authentication tag to detect a wrong passphrase or damaged content.

Todorbit does not save or upload your recovery passphrase or derived key. If you lose the passphrase, the backup cannot be recovered by Todorbit. Keep it separately from your backups.

Google receives encrypted backup bytes and unencrypted metadata: a backup identifier, backup kind, application/schema/format versions, encryption status, creation time and size. Downloads are decrypted locally. Opening a full backup for review creates an unencrypted local SQLite snapshot, even if you cancel replacing the active database. That staged snapshot is separate from the cloud copy. An approved restore creates local database and recovery files outside the encrypted cloud envelope.

Data transfers directly between your device and Google's API. Todorbit does not send Google account data or backup contents to an operator backend, advertisers or AI training services. Google API data is used only to provide the user-facing backup and recovery feature and its account-safety checks. Google handles its service under its own privacy policy.

5. Retention and deletion

Todorbit does not automatically delete cloud snapshots. They remain in your account until deleted. To remove one, open Settings > Backups & Cloud, connect the intended account, choose Delete on that snapshot and confirm. This permanently removes that snapshot; keep another recoverable copy before deleting.

Disconnect removes the saved session for this local profile. It does not delete cloud backups or revoke the Google authorization grant. Reconnect to manage retained snapshots. You can revoke access separately through Google Account connections. Where available, Google Drive's Settings > Manage apps also provides controls for hidden app data. Revocation alone should not be treated as confirmed snapshot deletion.

Local databases and recovery snapshots remain on your device independently of cloud deletion. Uninstalling the application is not a substitute for managing those files. Back up wanted data and verify the active profile before deleting any local files.

6. Updates, website and support

The optional application updater contacts GitHub for release metadata and downloads. No planner database is attached to an update request. GitHub processes those requests under its privacy statement.

This static website adds no analytics, tracking cookies, advertising scripts, contact forms or external fonts. If published on GitHub Pages, hosting requests are handled by GitHub under that privacy statement. Clicking a link to GitHub, Google or email opens that service, which has its own practices.

If you contact the maintainer or open a public GitHub issue, you choose what information to share. Use disposable examples and avoid private records, credentials or backup files. Security concerns can be reported by email.

7. Questions and changes

Contact hussamalkhatib24@gmail.com for privacy questions. Material changes to Google data use must be disclosed before that new use, with renewed consent where required. The published policy and in-app disclosures should describe the same behavior.
